mvpAdversarialAudit.notes: Endorsements pass: participant reacted with visible relief to the document-compilation/form-filling feature (cue 389) and was enthusiastic about tagging the bot in group channels (cue 424). General affect throughout the demo section was positive. Hesitations pass: one clear concern was raised proactively — information timeliness/accuracy (cue 352), before the Slack demo was even shown. No hesitations about privacy, AI tone, or AI for emotional support were expressed in response to the demo. Post-demo engagement was consistently curious and constructive. The one hesitation found is task-accuracy-based, not AI-skepticism-based.

summary:
INT003 is a non-binary, 41-year-old Altadena resident whose home sustained smoke and chemical contamination severe enough to require discarding nearly all contents, yet without the clarity of a total loss. This liminal status — structurally standing but chemically uninhabitable — defines their recovery. More than a year after the Eaton Fire, they remain displaced in a Highland Park rental found through community connections, and are locked in an adversarial legal battle with State Farm that has required hiring lawyers.

A former JPL engineer who worked on the Europa Clipper mission, INT003 was laid off in October 2025 due to federal budget cuts compounded by the fire's disruption. They describe the two events as inseparable: the combination of losing neighborhood, home usability, and career produced acute disorientation and identity loss. They are now exploring starting a community-focused business in Altadena — the first thing to spark genuine interest since the disaster.

Emotionally, INT003 frames the experience in terms of moral injury rather than mere misfortune. Two disabled neighbors perished after calling 911 multiple times and receiving no evacuation assistance. Combined with insurance failures and government inaction on contamination, this has produced deep anger at institutional betrayal that INT003 explicitly distinguishes from individual grief. The Altadena community — its tight-knit block culture, Facebook groups, and peer networks — has been the central emotional anchor and is central to why they chose to stay in the area rather than relocate.

Practically, inventory is the dominant ongoing burden: documenting every contaminated item for insurance and litigation purposes, hundreds of uncompensated hours, with physical health consequences (respiratory symptoms for a week or two after each visit) that limit how often INT003 can enter the home. Executive functioning impairment during peak recovery made simultaneous full-time work and recovery unsustainable, eventually leading to reduced hours and then the layoff.

Technology use is sophisticated and varied: Google Drive as comprehensive document hub, Facebook groups as real-time information lifeline, and AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini) deployed for photo-based inventory, assertive insurance letter drafting, and pre-call anxiety scaffolding. INT003 is a careful AI user who independently verified a hallucinated insurance code and explicitly names the risk to less tech-savvy survivors.

The MVP response was engaged and largely positive. The primary concern was information timeliness, raised proactively before the Slack demo was shown. INT003 was especially excited by the prospect of tagging the bot within existing group conversations. Notably, without any prompting, they raised an equity concern about tech tools being designed for already-resourced users while the most marginalized Altadena survivors may have no access at all.
